overview: Scoping review following JBI guidance for reviews that include quantitative and qualitative evidence, with a convergent segregated approach: strand A charts measured outcomes of prospective audit and feedback, strand B charts experience of recommendations; each strand has its own primary charted outcome and summary, set side by side in a joint display.
population: Reports from 2005 onward, in English or French, of hospital prospective audit and feedback (any ward or hospital size), including journal articles, theses and provincial or professional reports.
exposure: Prospective audit and feedback by a stewardship team, by delivery mode (in person, written, telephone) and setting (medical, surgical, intensive care, hospitals under 200 beds).
procedures: The library runs searches in three bibliographic databases and provincial health websites. Titles and abstracts are screened by the stewardship pharmacist, with the resident screening in duplicate from January and a second screening of the pre-January set at that point. Strand A reports are charted by the pharmacist with the resident verifying 20 percent; strand B reports are read and coded by the pharmacist and the fellow together. Charting forms are tested on the nine retrieved records.

outcomes.name: Strand A: antimicrobial use as reported
outcomes.measure: Charted use measure (days of therapy, length of therapy or defined daily doses), its denominator and the reported change
outcomes.why: The main measured result the committee asked for; measures differ (claim c6).

outcomes.name: Strand B: reasons recommendations are accepted or declined
outcomes.measure: Coded reasons for acceptance or refusal by professional group and setting
outcomes.why: The main experience result the committee asked for (claims c3, c4, c7).

outcomes.name: Strand A: acceptance rate and delivery mode
outcomes.measure: Charted acceptance proportion with delivery mode and caseload
outcomes.why: Links delivery to acceptance (claims c2, c5).

outcomes.name: Strand A: clinical outcomes with concurrent interventions
outcomes.measure: Charted C. difficile, mortality and readmission results with any concurrent policy
outcomes.why: Patient outcomes, read against confounding policies.

outcomes.name: Staffing and pharmacist time
outcomes.measure: Charted FTE, time per review and time per in-person discussion
outcomes.why: The committee must extend with the same staff.

outcomes.name: French-language and small-hospital reports
outcomes.measure: Count of included reports in French and from hospitals under 200 beds
outcomes.why: Shows how far the map reaches the community hospitals.

feasibility: About 70 pharmacist hours from October to March, 40 resident hours from January and 40 fellow hours; library searches confirmed.
biasMitigation: Strands charted and summarised separately before any side-by-side display
Charting forms tested on the nine retrieved records
Concurrent interventions charted next to every clinical outcome

biasFlags.label: Single screening before January
biasFlags.note: Records screened by one reviewer before January are rescreened by the resident.

biasFlags.label: Strand leakage
biasFlags.note: Experience findings must not be converted into numbers or numbers into themes.

flags: Two primary outcomes by design: one per strand, charted and reported separately and never combined
parsimony.simplestPath: Two questions, two charting forms, two summaries set side by side.

theoreticalFramework: JBI convergent segregated approach; no behavioural framework imposed on strand B coding beyond the committee's three themes (timing, hierarchy, delivery mode) plus inductive codes.
summary: Two-strand protocol with one primary charted outcome per strand, two secondary and two process measures.
